extracted.intended_audience: solo character comedians/performers seeking to audition for the JFL Character Showcases at the Annoyance theatre
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for auditioning to perform solo character comedy material in the JFL Character Showcases at the Annoyance. Covers required material, prior performance readiness, scheduling/availability, and where to find examples and sign-up information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material length requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Please prepare 6 minutes of original material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly instructs a 6-minute audition piece — prepare that length when signing up and performing at the audition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original material
rubrics_metrics.description: Please prepare 6 minutes of original material that would be pretty close to what you'd actually do if you were selected to be in JFL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material should be your own and reflect what you would present in the actual showcase (not an experimental or placeholder set).

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo character material only (no standup)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are looking only for solo character material, not standup, as standup showcases will be at other venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit traditional standup sets — the selection is specifically for character-based pieces. The organizers have been asked not to choose standups for these showcases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance-readiness / prior stage testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Please audition only if you have already put this material up in front of an audience and worked on it. You will be asked where you've put this up when you sign up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must have previously performed and refined the material; organizers will ask for where it has been performed. The page stresses not to audition if you are not ready and suggests waiting until next year if the material hasn't been stage-tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity to show-ready material
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare material that would be pretty close to what you'd actually do if you were selected to be in JFL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audition pieces should closely match the finished performance you intend to present in the showcase (i.e., minimal placeholder or unrehearsed content).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audition scheduling and sign-up timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditions will be held March 23rd & 24th from 11:30am - 6:30pm and March 25th from 3pm - 6:30pm. Audition link will be on this blog and will go live on Wednesday 2/7 at 11:30AM; it will also be posted on social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign up when the link goes live. Be prepared to select an audition slot within those stated date/time windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showcase dates and performance times
rubrics_metrics.description: Annoyance JFL Character Showcase dates: April 4th, 5PM and April 5th, 4PM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If selected, you will be expected to perform on one of these show dates; plan availability accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory tech rehearsal attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be a tech rehearsal the day of each showcase that you must be available to attend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tech rehearsal times given: April 4 tech rehearsal 1:00–4:30 PM; April 5 tech rehearsal 12:00–3:30 PM. Availability for the full tech window on the show day is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use example performances as models
rubrics_metrics.description: To see an example of what your audition should look like, check out this JFL New Faces- Characters video on YouTube - there are others as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch the referenced example videos to understand the expected style, format, and production level of successful character showcase auditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not audition if not ready
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't audition if you're not ready - there's nothing wrong with taking the time to work on your material and signing up next year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is explicit guidance to avoid submitting undeveloped work; organizers prefer polished, stage-tested pieces and encourage waiting rather than presenting unfinished material.
